question: In what ratio should tea costing Rs. 90 per kg be mixed with tea costing Rs. 150 per kg so that by selling the mixture for Rs. 143 per kg there is a profit of 30%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price (CP) of the mixture = 143 × 100 / 130 = Rs. 110.

By using the rule of alligation:

Ratio = (Dearer Price − Mean Price) : (Mean Price − Cheaper Price)

Ratio = (150 − 110) : (110 − 90) = 40 : 20 = 2 : 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 ∶ 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

CP of first tea (CP₁) = Rs. 90/kg

CP of second tea (CP₂) = Rs. 150/kg

Selling Price (SP) of mixture = Rs. 143/kg

Profit percentage = 30%

Formula used:

CP = [SP × 100] / [100 + Profit%]

 
 CP1 (90)
 
 
 CP2 (150)
 
 
 110
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 150−110 = 40
 110−90 = 20
 
 Ratio = 40 : 20 = 2 : 1

Calculations:

⇒ Mean CP of mixture = (143 × 100) / (100 + 30)

⇒ Mean CP = (143 × 100) / 130

⇒ Mean CP = 11 × 10 = Rs. 110

⇒ According to Alligation Rule:

⇒ (Quantity of tea 1) / (Quantity of tea 2) = (CP₂ − Mean CP) / (Mean CP − CP₁)

⇒ Ratio = (150 − 110) / (110 − 90)

⇒ Ratio = 40 / 20

⇒ Ratio = 2 / 1

**∴ The correct answer is 2 ∶ 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rule of Alligation

It is used to find the ratio in which two or more ingredients at given prices must be mixed to produce a mixture of a specified price.

Profit and CP Relation

When profit is made, CP = SP / (1 + Profit/100). Always ensure all prices used in the alligation cross (CP1, CP2, and Mean Price) are in the same unit (all must be Cost Prices).

Weighted Average

Mean Price = (n₁ × c₁ + n₂ × c₂) / (n₁ + n₂), where n is quantity and c is price per unit.
